metadata.methods_description: Six EEG runs per participant: resting-state runs of 300 s at the start and end, and four runs of 10 music-listening trials each. Stimuli were 12 s film-score excerpts from Eerola & Vuoskoski stimulus set 1, rated for induced emotion. EEG was sampled at 1 kHz.

citation_details.title: Affective Neural Responses Sonified through Labeled Correlation Alignment
citation_details.author: Andrés Marino Álvarez-Meza, Héctor Fabio Torres-Cardona, Mauricio Orozco‐Alzate, Hernán Darío Pérez-Nastar, German Castellanos-Dominguez
citation_details.abstract: Sound synthesis refers to the creation of original acoustic signals with broad applications in artistic innovation, such as music creation for games and videos. Nonetheless, machine learning architectures face numerous challenges when learning musical structures from arbitrary corpora. This issue involves adapting patterns borrowed from other contexts to a concrete composition objective. Using Labeled Correlation Alignment (LCA), we propose an approach to sonify neural responses to affective music-listening data, identifying the brain features that are most congruent with the simultaneously extracted auditory features. For dealing with inter/intra-subject variability, a combination of Phase Locking Value and Gaussian Functional Connectivity is employed. The proposed two-step LCA approach embraces a separate coupling stage of input features to a set of emotion label sets using Centered Kernel Alignment. This step is followed by canonical correlation analysis to select multimodal representations with higher relationships. LCA enables physiological explanation by adding a backward transformation to estimate the matching contribution of each extracted brain neural feature set. Correlation estimates and partition quality represent performance measures. The evaluation uses a Vector Quantized Variational AutoEncoder to create an acoustic envelope from the tested Affective Music-Listening database. Validation results demonstrate the ability of the developed LCA approach to generate low-level music based on neural activity elicited by emotions while maintaining the ability to distinguish between the acoustic outputs.

citation_details.title: Not all generalisation failures can be bought back: four boundaries in affective audio modelling
citation_details.author: Jingyi Zhang, Xiaotong Yao
citation_details.abstract: Analysis code, run records, figure sources and manuscript for a multi-corpus study of how far a mapping from acoustic descriptors to human affective response survives four changes of setting — new material, edited audio, a sensor in place of a self-report, and an individual listener — and of what each adaptation route tested recovers when it does not. This archive supersedes an earlier preprint (arXiv:2608.27674), whose organising claim — that generalisation failures divide into two kinds with mutually exclusive remedies — is contradicted by this project's own measurements and is withdrawn. reports/TAC_revision_audit.md records what was withdrawn, corrected and recomputed, and what remains a stated limitation. Two findings concern corpora in wide use and are useful independently of the main result. In Emo-Soundscapes, 613 of 1,213 clips are mixtures of thirty source recordings, and the distributed metadata gives every clip its own group identifier, so grouped cross-validation on the supplied groups provides no protection against near-duplicates spanning folds. In PMEmo, a sham using presentation position alone reproduces 114–249% of the stimulus-level reliability of its song-level electrodermal measures. Licensing. Code is MIT (see LICENSE); manuscript text and figures are CC BY 4.0. The nine analysed corpora are third-party and are not redistributed here — several carry non-commercial terms and one has no audio redistribution right at all. Per-corpus terms, including whether derived files may be redistributed, are in DATA_LICENSES.md; read it before reusing anything built from them. Reproducibility, stated plainly. The run records fix the script, the seed, the parameters and the resulting metrics. They do not pin the code: records were written from working trees with uncommitted changes, input hashes cover a minority of runs and output hashes are absent. The analyses reproduce from the scripts at the recorded parameters; they do not yet reproduce bit-for-bit from a pinned commit.

citation_details.title: What masking geometry works best for EEG foundation models?
citation_details.author: Pierre Guetschel, Bruno Aristimunha, Yassine El Ouahidi, Arnaud Delorme, Thomas Moreau, Michael Tangermann
citation_details.abstract: EEG foundation models hold promise for scalable brain-signal decoding across clinical and cognitive neuroscience applications, yet their pre-training pipelines remain poorly understood. Among design choices, the masking strategy is particularly critical: it determines what the network must predict and from which context. Yet it has never been ablated in isolation, as each new model bundles a new masking strategy with a new backbone and objective. In this paper, we formalize the design choices for spatio-temporal masking strategies and train various models with a single pipeline under varying masking configurations across two SSL frameworks (MAE and JEPA). We then systematically evaluate the resulting 58 pre-trained models on the 12 datasets of OpenEEGBench under a linear probe. Both frameworks agree on an optimal masking configuration and on shared failure modes. Outside these, performance is robust: 11 MAE and 9 JEPA configurations are statistically indistinguishable from the best. We further identify a novel JEPA-specific failure mode, tagged bias-inflation collapse, invisible to standard detectors. With a well-chosen mask, our pipeline reaches REVE-level downstream performance at a fraction of REVE's pre-training compute.

citation_details.title: Geometric Obstruction to Navier-Stokes Singularities via Lo Shu-Merkaba-E8 Structure: A Four-Layer Framework with EEG Empirical Validation
citation_details.author: Yao-Kai Kao
citation_details.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
citation_details.abstract: We present a four-layer geometric framework addressing Navier-Stokes singularity formation. Layer 1 (proved): Any NS singularity must be self-similar, requiring continuous SO(3) rotational symmetry. Layer 2 (proved): The Merkaba-E8 structure admits only discrete rotations (octahedral group O, 24 elements). Since SO(3) is not a subgroup of O, this constitutes a topological obstruction. Layer 3 (numerically confirmed): The E8 geometric energy achieves its global maximum at the magic angle theta_m = arccos(1/sqrt(3)) ≈ 54.74°, co-located (within 2.74°) with the NS singularity sink zone, creating an energy barrier ΔE ≥ 7.5. Layer 4 (empirical, phenomenological): Analysis of real EEG data (OpenNeuro ds002721, 30-45 Hz Gamma, 304 s) reveals statistically significant magic-angle locking (Monte Carlo p = 0.0004) with strong antipodal phase coherence (APC ≈ -0.83), providing phenomenological evidence that E8 magic-angle geometry is imprinted in real neural Gamma dynamics.

citation_details.title: Geometric Obstruction and Bootstrap Closure of Navier-Stokes Singularities via E8 Symmetry
citation_details.author: Yao-Kai Kao
citation_details.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
citation_details.abstract: We present a complete logical framework for the global regularity of the Navier-Stokes (NS) equations by synthesizing a Bootstrap Strategy with the E8 geometric obstruction theory. The framework has four established layers: (L1) Any NS singularity requires continuous SO(3) rotational symmetry. (L2) The Merkaba-E8 structure admits only discrete rotations (SO(3) not subset of O), providing a topological obstruction. (L3) The E8 energy barrier ΔE ≥ 7.5 is numerically confirmed. (L4) Real EEG data (OpenNeuro ds002721, p=0.0004, APC≈-0.83) confirms magic-angle locking. The Bootstrap Strategy shows that if 2× geometric deformation is bounded, fractal self-similarity of NS scaling guarantees all scales are safe. The entire framework reduces to a single open conjecture: C_bil ≤ 4√3/(15√2) ≈ 0.327. Honest scope: L1-L2 are mathematically proved. L3 is numerically confirmed. L4 is phenomenological. The Bootstrap closes conditionally on the bilinear conjecture.

citation_details.title: MMSI Neuro v3.6 - Native Android Validation Framework
citation_details.author: Patrick Frank Buckreus
citation_details.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
citation_details.abstract: 🧬 MMSI Neuro Clinical Assessment Suite — Release v1.0.0-clinical Initial Clinical Baseline Release | Synchronisiert mit MMSI Core Engine v3.6.4 📌 Übersicht & Anwendungsbereich Dieses Repository enthält die dedizierte Clinical Assessment Suite des MMSI Neuro Frameworks. Das System dient der automatisierten Ingestion, Auswertung und Befundgenerierung von vielkanaligen EEG-Trajektorien zur Detektion kognitiver Instabilitäten (u. a. Schizophrenie-Profile im Vergleich zu gesunden Kontrollgruppen). 🛠️ Schlüsselkomponenten & Systemarchitektur 1. Multi-Probanden Batch Ingestion & Dynamic Clipping Fix Dynamic Bounds Regularization: Beseitigung mathematischer Sättigungsartefakte ($W(t) = 5.800$, $\sigma^2 = 0$) durch adaptive Varianzpartitionierung im EegViewModel. OpenNeuro & PhysioNet Data Pipeline: Native Ingestion-Schnittstellen für anonymisierte klinische Datensätze (z. B. OpenNeuro ds002721). 2. Automated PDF Assessment Generator Vector-to-Bitmap Pipeline: Automatische Generierung von hochauslösenden PNG-Visualisierungen der kognitiven Lasttrajektorie $W(t)$. Klinischer Befundbericht: Vollautomatische Erstellung strukturierter Multi-Seiten-PDF-Befunde inklusive statistischer Kennzahlen (Mittelwert, Varianz, RMSD, Verweildauer $>3.2$, Diagnostic Score). 3. M3-Dashboard & Operational UX Drei-Zonen-Konditionierung: Strikt entkoppeltes UI-Konzept (Status-Ingestion, Trajektorien-Visualisierung, System-Steuerung). Signal Health Monitoring: Visuelles Real-Time-Badge zur Indikation von Grenzwertüberschreitungen. 🔬 Empirische Validierung (Clinical Dataset N=10) Der Veröffentlichungsstand wurde gegen 10 klassifizierte Probandenprofile validiert: Healthy Controls (SUB-001, 003, 005, 008): Homöostatisch stabil ($W(t) \approx 0.86 - 1.03$, Status: STABIL). Pathological Profiles (SUB-002, 006, 009, 010): Hochgradige multivariate Instabilität ($W(t) > 3.2$, Status: PATHOLOGISCH, Diagnostic Score $>98%$). Borderline Profiles (SUB-004, 007): Transient abweichende Trajektorien-Dynamik (Status: GRENZWERT). 📦 Kompilierte Artefakte & Nachweise Android App Binary: app-release.apk (Baugleiche Standalone-Instanz für mobile Testreihen) Clinical Validation Report: MMSI_Clinical_Batch_Report.pdf DOI Archivierung: Versiegelt via CERN/Zenodo (DOI-Zuordnung erfolgt automatisch durch Release-Tag)
